title: Layout and panes
body:
decade's panes are three fixed rectangles in `src/server/panes.rs`, each with a
title strip, and a client that exits leaves its rectangle empty for good.
This milestone makes the layout a tree the user can change, with as few
keys as possible, and settles what a pane is for.

Decided with Jack on 2026-11-06:

- Three keys, no more for now: Ctrl+h, j, k, l focus; Ctrl+Space opens the
  command palette; Ctrl+Shift+Enter makes a new pane. No close, resize, zoom
  or swap keys. decade is not a keybind-driven program; the TUI inspiration
  stops at the visuals and the multiplexing.
- A pane is a rectangle with a one-cell outline and nothing else. Only the
  focused pane's outline is coloured.
- Closing is the client's job (Ctrl+d at a shell). The fallback is the Ctrl
  bar: holding Ctrl alone shows a one-row bar at the top of every pane with
  the name, a zoom toggle and an X, for the mouse. The bar pushes the client
  down a row rather than covering it.
- Anchors: a pane can be a home for a program, matched by a rule, that stays
  as an empty slot saying what it waits for when the client exits. A
  transient pane closes with its client. This is the core of the dev loop
  where a GUI app is opened and closed over and over and should land in the
  same place each time. Anchors must eventually be set up over MCP so agents
  can arrange them.

## Pieces

| Issue | Role |
|---|---|
| split tree, anchors, new pane | the model: tree, two pane kinds, placement rules, Ctrl+Shift+Enter |
| Ctrl bar | hold Ctrl alone to show per-pane bars with zoom and close |
| gutter drag | drag the boundary between two panes to resize |
| scroll wheel | forward pointer axis events to clients |
| palette stub | Ctrl+Space opens an empty palette that Esc closes, so the key is claimed |
| drag to swap | later: drag a bar onto another pane to swap |
| pin | later: a bar toggle that turns a transient pane into an anchor |
| anchors over MCP | later: tools to list, create and change anchors |
| saved sessions | later: a session is a tree of anchors with rules |

## Out of scope

- A visual design beyond the outline. That is Jack's.
- Workspaces or tabs. One tree per window for now.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/618aab71
notes.text: State on 2026-11-06 at commit 93a5286: the split tree, anchors, transient panes, Ctrl bar, gutter drag, axis forwarding and palette stub are in. Outlines are box-drawing glyphs in colours from src/palette.rs, copied from the Omarchy theme. Focus is fast again: a focus change reconfigures only the two panes involved and the chrome texture is patched for changed cells only (GlesRenderer::update_memory reads a region out of a full-size buffer, so the chrome pixels are kept beside the texture). The dev profile builds at opt-level 1. Checked by Jack by hand: focus by key and mouse. Not yet checked by hand: the bar's buttons, boundary drag, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, the palette, scroll. Known: the bar appears too slowly, filed as its own bug.
